mcqs.question: How does the chapter separate lymphangitic carcinomatosis from pulmonary tumor embolism?

options.A: Lymphangitic disease is mainly interstitial, without tumor cells in pulmonary arteries or capillaries; tumor embolism has tumor cells inside the vessels
options.B: They are different names for left-heart failure
options.D: Tumor embolism is always interstitial and never intravascular
options.E: The chapter says they cannot be distinguished pathologically at all

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Lymphangitic disease is mainly interstitial, without tumor cells in pulmonary arteries or capillaries; tumor embolism has tumor cells inside the vessels
mcqs.explanation: The chapter says lymphangitic carcinomatosis is predominantly interstitial with absent tumor cells in pulmonary arteries or capillaries, whereas tumor embolism has tumor cells inside the vessels.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The terms pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis & pulmonary tumor embolism represent end-stage manifestations of malignancies and have been used synonymously in the literature given highly similar clinical & radiological features though the former represents a pathology predominantly restricted to the interstitium with absent tumor cells in pulmonary arteries and or capillaries, whereas the latter demonstrates the presence of tumor cells inside the pulmonary vessels.

mcqs.question: What share of pulmonary metastases, and what histology, does the chapter give?

options.A: About 6 to 8 percent of pulmonary metastases are lymphangitic, and about 80 percent of those are adenocarcinomas
options.B: Half of all metastases are squamous
options.C: Lymphangitic spread causes most pulmonary metastases

mcqs.correctAnswerText: About 6 to 8 percent of pulmonary metastases are lymphangitic, and about 80 percent of those are adenocarcinomas
mcqs.explanation: Only about 6 to 8 percent of pulmonary metastasis is lymphangitic carcinomatosis, and 80 percent of that is adenocarcinoma.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Only about 6 -8 % of pulmonary metastasis is caused by lymphangitic carcinomatosis. 80 % of pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis is caused by adenocarcinomas.

mcqs.question: What is described as the commonest presentation?

options.A: Dyspnea evolving over days to weeks
options.C: A single episode of syncope as the only symptom

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Dyspnea evolving over days to weeks
mcqs.explanation: Dyspnea evolving over days to weeks is the commonest presentation, in almost 60 percent of patients.

sourceRefs.excerpt: dyspnea, which evolves over days to weeks, is the commonest presentation in almost 60 % of patients.

mcqs.question: What CT pattern does the chapter describe?

options.A: Smooth thickening of interlobular septa and peribronchovascular interstitium early, and nodular thickening later
options.C: A normal scan in every case
options.E: A solitary round nodule without septal thickening

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Smooth thickening of interlobular septa and peribronchovascular interstitium early, and nodular thickening later
mcqs.explanation: CT shows smooth septal and peribronchovascular thickening early, and nodular thickening later.

sourceRefs.excerpt: CT thorax: Interlobular septa & peribronchovascular interstitium exhibits smooth (early stage), or nodular thickening(late development).

mcqs.question: What life expectancy does the chapter attach to the diagnosis, before noting longer survivors?

options.B: About six days in every case
options.D: More than 10 years as the usual course

mcqs.explanation: The chapter says life expectancy is about six months, and also notes reports of survival up to 3 years.

sourceRefs.excerpt: life expectancy being about six months.
